candidates.spoken: Avalanches failed because weak-layer collapse under a snow slab.
It explodes downhill at eighty miles an hour.
The real cause was weak-layer collapse under a snow slab.
The slope was not the problem.
Snow falls in layers all winter long.
Between them sits a weak, sugary layer of crystals.
One extra load snaps that bond and the slab slides.
Slopes near thirty eight degrees are the most dangerous.
A single skier can bring down thousands of tons of snow.
It started with weak layer buried. It ended with slab releases.
It holds the slab above like a house of cards.
In most avalanche deaths the victims triggered the slide themselves.
